provenance.writtenFor: DAST app-surface batch 5 (2026-10-21): negative controls for the debug-surface and build-configuration batch
provenance.kind: synthetic test fixture - NOT vulnerability intelligence

purpose: A handbook that names every toolbar, dev UI and build file in its own batch must stay silent, because a file name is not a served file.

groundTruth.rationale: The page lists every product and artefact the batch detects, but it serves none of them: no toolbar container, no development chunk path, no configuration body and no shell history. A detector that fires here is matching vocabulary rather than a response shape.

observation.body:
Local development only

  • Debug toolbars (Django, Flask, Rails web console) must stay in the development group.
  • We never serve a development build: no Next.js development chunks, no Nuxt devtools overlay and no Astro toolbar in production.
  • Dev UIs such as Quarkus q-dev and Spring Boot Admin sit behind the bastion.
  • Runtime diagnostics: the Go expvar handler, TensorBoard, MLflow, Prefect, Dagster, the Flink dashboard, the Storm UI and the YARN ResourceManager are internal services.
  • Build configuration (.yarnrc, Gemfile.lock, yarn.lock, composer.lock, poetry.lock, go.mod, the Terraform provider lockfile, a Jenkinsfile, GitLab CI and Travis definitions) is excluded from every release artefact.
  • Server internals (the Apache server-info page), local settings, development appsettings and shell or SSH material (.bash_history, authorized_keys) are never inside the document root.

limitations: Observation mode: a synthetic response object, not a live target.
The names appear in prose only, so a rule that fires here is reading a keyword rather than the file or interface it claims to find.
